profile.headline: Software Developer at IBM
profile.summary: Experienced IT Professional in roles of Product Development, Professional Services and Support.

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Developing a Kubernetes based microservice platform for the Storage Defender data resiliency solution.
Implementing agents to support inventory and recovery for Flash Storage, VMWare, Data Protect and others.
Lead hands-on engineering for integration between Storage Protect Plus and Storage Protect products.
Lead Hypervisor Development Team of 6 engineers on the IBM Storage Protect Plus product.
Mentoring new developers and teams on existing tools, practices and code base.

positions.title: Principal Software Engineer
positions.description:
Senior backend developer for IBM Spectrum Protect Plus
Development experience with Java (Spring), Python, REST, Kubernetes, Go, js and MongoDB
Design, architecture, and development of vCenter and ServiceNow plugins
Primary engineer for AWS EC2, VMWare and Hyper-V areas of product integration 
Triage, troubleshooting and bugfixes for both QA and critical customer issues
Pre and post sales engineering tasks, such as scripting or custom integrations

positions.title: Solutions Engineer
positions.description:
Customer facing engineer for ECX and SCDM copy data management platforms
Assisting with pre and post sales activity from a technical perspective
SME for RESTful API, automation, scripting, and integration

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Full stack software engineer for Quantum MES product
Back-end work with Java/Spring, SQL, Oracle/PLSQL
Front end work with JavaScript, YUI, HTML, CSS
Also filled roles of professional services engineer and technical project lead.

positions.title: Client Technical Analyst IV
positions.description:
Technical support for automotive dealership finance software
Experience troubleshooting complex software/hardware issues and managing challenging customer interactions
SME for digital contracting product suite.
